bullets.title: META +8.8%: Cloud compute monetization story dominates — Bulls cite $20B+ ARR optionality, Bears see capex desperation
bullets.body: META surged ~8.8% on Bloomberg reports it is building 'Meta Compute' to sell excess AI infrastructure capacity (GPU access + model APIs, similar to AWS Bedrock). Bulls: KeyBanc (OW, $760 PT) sees $20B+ ARR upside and improved capex ROI; Citi (Buy, $850 PT) calls it FCF-accretive; Mizuho (OP, $835 PT) views it as 2027-28 optionality; Morgan Stanley (OW, $775 PT) estimates every 250MW leased generates ~$3 EPS accretion in '28. Bear case (Oppenheimer): excess capacity signals advertising slowdown and failed frontier LLM strategy. Meta's Muse models underperformed on key benchmarks vs. Gemini.

bullets.title: CRWV -14%, NBIS -15%: META compute announcement is direct competitive threat to neoclouds
bullets.body: CoreWeave (CRWV) fell ~14% and Nebius (NBIS) fell ~15% as markets priced in META as a direct neocloud competitor. DA Davidson flags NBIS has META as >50% of backlog and CRWV at ~33%; JPM characterizes the selloff as positioning/de-grossing rather than a fundamental demand shift. DA Davidson views NVDA and GOOGL as largely insulated, while AMD and AVGO face more vulnerability if META scales back third-party GPU demand.

bullets.title: Semis/Memory selloff: MU -10.6%, SOX -6.3% on META neocloud fears and momentum unwind
bullets.body: Semiconductor index fell 6.3% led by MU -10.6% after its ~88% SOX rally in H1; SNDK also down sharply. DA Davidson argues MU selloff is unwarranted — fundamentals remain positive at 8x earnings with DRAM spot prices up 8x YoY after three consecutive monthly gains and NAND still 5x higher YoY. DRAM/NAND strength driven by HBM skew toward AI servers. JPM LLM token demand re-accelerating: June volumes up 70% MoM, 20x YoY.

bullets.title: AAPL: Cutting iPhone 17 production; in talks with Chinese memory suppliers CXMT/YMTC
bullets.body: Apple is reducing iPhone 17 production plans amid lower shipment forecasts, while simultaneously in talks with Pentagon-blacklisted Chinese chipmakers CXMT and YMTC for China-market memory chips and lobbying White House for support. Memory/storage prices have quadrupled in three quarters; Counterpoint estimates higher component costs could add ~$200/iPhone. Apple has already announced 15-33% price hikes across Mac/iPad/HomePod lines citing supply constraints.

bullets.title: MSFT: Job cuts next week impacting thousands; stock +3% as software/internet outperforms
bullets.body: Microsoft is reportedly announcing thousands of job cuts next week (described as less than 2.5% of workforce), yet MSFT shares gained ~3% on the day as software and internet sectors broadly outperformed while semis lagged. No analyst rating change noted.

bullets.title: BE: Expanded Brookfield AI infrastructure partnership to $25B from $5B; UBS raises PT to $355
bullets.body: Bloom Energy expanded its AI infrastructure partnership with Brookfield to $25B (from $5B), with Brookfield's AI Infrastructure Fund targeting $100B deployment total. UBS reiterated Buy and raised its price target to $355 from $322. Utilities sector was broadly weak (S&P Utilities Index -1.3%), with IPPs TLN -6.1%, VST -3.5%, CEG -4.8%.

bullets.title: FOXA upgraded to Outperform at Wolfe; APP extends rally after Raymond James strong buy; WBD merger progresses
bullets.body: FOXA upgraded to Outperform at Wolfe Research, with the Roku merger shifting narrative to multichannel growth (+3.8%). APP extended gains after Monday's Raymond James strong buy initiation citing e-commerce advertising growth opportunity (+9.6% on day). PSKY received unconditional regulatory approvals from Kuwait, Austria, and Australia for WBD takeover; submitted EU commitments. CMCSA declined after announcing plan to spin off media business.

bullets.title: CRM and NOW both upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim
bullets.body: Salesforce (CRM) upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim with a $228 PT, with the AI bear case called a 'hallucination.' ServiceNow (NOW) also upgraded to Buy at Guggenheim with a $125 PT on valuation and double-digit growth trajectory. Both names benefited from the broader software/internet outperformance day (+3.1% sector).

bullets.title: AFRM: Citi raises PT to $115; FY29 EPS upside case to $5.00 (+34% vs consensus)
bullets.body: Citi raises AFRM price target to $115 with a FY29 GAAP EPS upside scenario of $5.00 vs. consensus $3.72, driven by 30% GMV growth (vs. 25%+ midterm target) from new merchants (Intuit, ServiceTitan, Lowe's, Costco) and Affirm card, RLTC margins at high end of 4% range, and 30% GAAP operating margin. Company expected to exceed 4Q26 guidance with 300+ bps GMV and revenue upside; FY27 guidance expected at 29% GMV growth.

bullets.title: TSLA: Q2 deliveries estimated at ~396K, tracking toward a beat per Morgan Stanley
bullets.body: Tesla's Q2 2026 deliveries are estimated at approximately 396,466 vehicles globally, with Morgan Stanley flagging the quarter is tracking toward a beat. Near-term energy storage solutions (ESS) outlook remains conservative per MS.

bullets.title: PLTR: CEO says 'something has gone completely wrong' with OpenAI/Anthropic token models
bullets.body: Palantir CEO made pointed comments that something has fundamentally gone wrong with OpenAI and Anthropic's token model approaches. No analyst rating action tied to the comment, but it received prominent placement in afternoon market summaries alongside Uber dismissing two tech leaders at its AI data labeling business.

bullets.title: HOOD: Added to Mizuho July Top Picks list as new #1 addition
bullets.body: Robinhood Markets (HOOD) was added to Mizuho's July Top Picks list as one of the new #1 additions for the month. The 28-stock list is bottom-up, analyst-driven highest-conviction ideas with a 12-month outlook; no specific PT or thesis detail was provided beyond the addition.

bullets.title: BABA: To pay $600M to settle DOJ probe over illegal substance sales on payment platform
bullets.body: Alibaba Group and its digital payment processor AUS Merchant Services agreed to pay $600M to settle a U.S. DOJ probe related to allegations of not preventing the illegal sale and importation of controlled substances and pharmaceuticals. BABA shares were up ~$2.46 to $98.45 at the time of the announcement.

bullets.title: Jefferies semis analyst raises PTs across AI infrastructure names ahead of earnings; BUY on NVDA ($300), AVGO ($550), ALAB ($270), CRDO ($270)
bullets.body: Jefferies' Blayne Curtis is hosting NYC investor meetings July 8 and carries BUY ratings on AMD ($515 PT), AVGO ($550), ALAB ($270), CRDO ($270), LITE ($1,200), MTSI ($450), MRVL ($325), NVDA ($300), SNDK ($3,000), and PI ($175). HOLDs on INTC ($120) and TXN ($260). Focus on AI accelerator and networking/optical spend and WFE trends expected to move higher.

bullets.title: GS desk: Semis extended on AI upside; exchanges (ICE/CME/CBOE) oversold after BTC futures approval; STX lagging WDC
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs equities desk notes semiconductor sentiment is meaningfully higher (AMAT +62%, LRCX +35% YTD) as investors shift upstream in AI value chain. Exchanges sold off ~20% on CFTC approval of BTC perpetual futures and are now viewed as oversold. STX is noted as lagging WDC recently with ongoing debate on the bull case. SPOT/DASH/RDDT weakness also flagged as ongoing discussion.

bullets.title: IREN: To be acquired by RKLB per Morgan Stanley digest
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's peer reading digest flagged that IREN is to be acquired by Rocket Lab (RKLB). No further deal terms or analyst rating action included in the note.

bullets.title: Hedge funds rotated out of TMT into cyclicals in June; net sold equities for first time in 3 months
bullets.body: Global fundamental L/S managers achieved record-breaking Q2 2026 performance, then net sold global equities in June for the first time in three months — led by short sales. Gross and net leverage fell, led by US and Asia L/S managers. Sector rotation: out of Info Tech and Comm Services, into Cyclicals in US positioning.

bullets.title: JPM maintains tactical bullish call with Tech/Cyclicals barbell; adds Healthcare as low-correlated long into earnings
bullets.body: JPM's afternoon briefing maintains a tactical bullish stance with a Tech/Cyclicals barbell and adds Healthcare as a low-correlated long. Q2 earnings season fundamentals solid per FactSet: 12.1% revenue growth, 22.0% earnings growth, 14.1% margins expected. Period-end rebalancing largely complete; dip-buying behavior prevalent. Citi separately raised S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100 with 2026E earnings of $350 and 2027E of $400.

bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh dovish lean: AI productivity upside, inflation expectations declining, task force news coming
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh at ECB Sintra cited 'high 2s' productivity growth over past four quarters and flagged AI's 'huge implications for monetary policy.' He noted inflation expectations and risks have declined over the past four weeks, and signaled desire to eliminate the dot plot. Long-end Treasury yields rose 6bp on his comments. Former BoE Governor Mervyn King to co-chair Fed communications task force; staffing announcement expected next week.

bullets.title: JPM semi/hyperscaler divergence note: semiconductor outperformance vs hyperscalers viewed as unsustainable
bullets.body: JPM flags semiconductors have outperformed hyperscalers steadily since September 2025, which it views as unsustainable. Hyperscalers posted record 100% YoY capex growth in 2026 but equity prices are flat and credit spreads have widened vs. semis. Short interest in hyperscalers rising steeply in May-June. Base case requires hyperscalers to successfully monetize AI; consensus sees sharp capex deceleration from 2027 as the key risk scenario.
